title: Hadwiger's Conjecture (Conjecture 1)
statement_text: For every integer $t\geq 2$, if $G$ is a graph which does not contain $K_{t}$ as a minor, then $\chi(G)\leq t-1$.
context_text: Hadwiger's conjecture is described as perhaps the most important open problem in graph coloring. The entire paper is motivated by developing a hypergraph analogue of this conjecture, generalizing the notion of graph minors to hypergraphs and studying the resulting chromatic bounds.
paper_contribution: Proves a weak hypergraph extension: for every $t\geq 1$ there exists a finite integer $h(t)$ such that every hypergraph with no $K_t$-minor is $h(t)$-colorable, and establishes $\left\lceil\frac{3}{2}(t-1)\right\rceil\leq h(t)\leq 2g(t)$ where $g(t)$ is the maximum chromatic number of $K_t$-minor-free graphs.

title: Conjecture 2
statement_text: For every integer $t\geq 2$ we have $h(t)=\left\lceil\frac{3}{2}(t-1)\right\rceil$. In other words, if a hypergraph $H$ does not contain $K_{t}$ as a minor, then $\chi(H)\leq\left\lceil\frac{3}{2}(t-1)\right\rceil$.
context_text: A hypergraph is a finite vertex set with a set of hyperedges, each a subset of size at least $2$ (no loops). A proper colouring assigns colours to vertices so that no hyperedge is monochromatic, and $\chi(H)$ is the least number of colours needed (the usual chromatic number for graphs). A set $W$ of vertices is connected if for every partition of $W$ into non-empty $X,Y$ some hyperedge contained in $W$ meets both $X$ and $Y$. $H_2$ is a minor of $H_1$ if it can be obtained from $H_1$ by repeatedly taking subhypergraphs and contracting a hyperedge $e$ (identifying all vertices of $e$ into one vertex, discarding hyperedges contained in $e$ and merging parallel copies). Equivalently, $H_1$ contains a $K_t$ minor if there are $t$ disjoint non-empty connected sets $B_1,\dots,B_t$ such that for all $i\ne j$ some hyperedge is contained in $B_i\cup B_j$ and meets both. $h(t)$ denotes the largest chromatic number of a hypergraph with no $K_t$ minor, and $g(t)$ the analogue for graphs (Hadwiger's conjecture says $g(t)=t-1$). The author shows $h(t)$ is finite with $\lceil\frac32(t-1)\rceil\le h(t)\le 2g(t)$, hence $h(t)=O(t\log\log t)$ by the Delcourt–Postle bound on $g(t)$; so Hadwiger's conjecture does not extend verbatim to hypergraphs. The lower bound comes from the complete $3$-uniform hypergraph on $3(t-1)$ vertices, which has no $K_t$ minor and chromatic number $\lceil\frac32(t-1)\rceil$ (its independent sets have size at most $2$). The conjecture is proved for hypergraphs with independence number at most $2$, and remains open even for $t=3$, where the best known upper bound is $4$.

title: Problem 1
context_text: A hypergraph is a finite vertex set with a set of hyperedges, each a subset of size at least $2$ (no loops). A proper colouring assigns colours to vertices so that no hyperedge is monochromatic, and $\chi(H)$ is the least number of colours needed (the usual chromatic number for graphs). A set $W$ of vertices is connected if for every partition of $W$ into non-empty $X,Y$ some hyperedge contained in $W$ meets both $X$ and $Y$. $H_2$ is a minor of $H_1$ if it can be obtained from $H_1$ by repeatedly taking subhypergraphs and contracting a hyperedge $e$ (identifying all vertices of $e$ into one vertex, discarding hyperedges contained in $e$ and merging parallel copies). Equivalently, $H_1$ contains a $K_t$ minor if there are $t$ disjoint non-empty connected sets $B_1,\dots,B_t$ such that for all $i\ne j$ some hyperedge is contained in $B_i\cup B_j$ and meets both. $h(t)$ denotes the largest chromatic number of a hypergraph with no $K_t$ minor, and $g(t)$ the analogue for graphs (Hadwiger's conjecture says $g(t)=t-1$). The author conjectures $h(t)=\lceil\frac32(t-1)\rceil$ for all $t\ge2$, which for $t=3$ predicts that every $K_3$-minor-free hypergraph is $3$-colourable; the matching lower bound comes from the complete $3$-uniform hypergraph on $6$ vertices, which has no $K_3$ minor and chromatic number $3$. This is the smallest open case of the conjecture: the best known upper bound for $K_3$-minor-free hypergraphs is $4$, from the author's general bound $h(t)\le 2g(t)$ (with $g(3)=2$).
